# Procedural textures and icons

Original visual assets for **Mosteiro do Sino Partido**, generated entirely
by the code in this folder. No photographs, scans, stock textures, fonts or
third-party artwork are used as input; every pixel and every path is
computed from fixed random seeds.

**License / provenance:** original work, generated by project code. The
outputs carry the same license as the rest of this repository.

## Rebuild

From the repository root:

```sh
python3 tools/python/textures/build_textures.py      # ~50 s, all textures + manifest
python3 tools/python/textures/build_icons.py         # ~3 s, all icons + sprite + manifest
python3 -m pytest tools/python/textures -q           # asset checks
```

Partial rebuilds: `build_textures.py stone_floor wax rune_ring` (any set or
sprite names; the manifest is merged). Previews:

```sh
python3 tools/python/textures/build_textures.py --contact /tmp/pbr.png          # PBR maps + lit 2x2 tiling preview
python3 tools/python/textures/build_textures.py --sprite-contact /tmp/fx.png    # helper sprites
python3 tools/python/textures/build_icons.py --contact /tmp/icons.png --px 96   # needs cairosvg
```

Dependencies: Python 3.11+, numpy, scipy, Pillow, shapely (icons). cairosvg
is optional and only used for icon contact sheets. Output is deterministic
for a given library version.

## Files

| file | role |
| --- | --- |
| `texlib.py` | periodic noise and map utilities shared by all textures |
| `build_textures.py` | PBR material sets, contact sheet, manifest writer |
| `sprites.py` | particles, decals, VFX rings, stained glass, UI images |
| `iconlib.py` | small vector-geometry DSL on top of shapely |
| `build_icons.py` | every icon definition, SVG/sprite/manifest writer |
| `test_assets.py` | pytest checks for both output folders |

Outputs:

* `apps/web/public/assets/textures/` + `manifest.json` (file, set, kind, size, bytes, colour space, tileable, purpose)
* `apps/web/public/assets/icons/<id>.svg`, `icons.svg` (sprite), `manifest.json` (id -> file, category, description)

## Texture technique

**Seamless by construction.** Everything is built on the unit torus, so
tiles wrap exactly; there is no cross-fading or mirroring.

* *Gradient noise* (`Perlin`, `fbm`, `ridged`): the lattice of random
  gradients has an integer period, so noise sampled at `u` and `u + 1` is
  identical. Domain warping keeps periodicity because the warp is itself
  periodic noise.
* *Spectral noise* (`spectral`): white noise shaped in the FFT domain by a
  `1/f^beta` envelope. FFT synthesis is inherently periodic; anisotropic
  weighting (`ax`, `ay`) produces wood fibres, soot streaks and rust runs.
* *Cellular noise* (`worley`, `voronoi_edge`): `scipy.spatial.cKDTree` with
  `boxsize=1` gives distances on the torus. Distance to a cell border uses the
  bisector formula `(|d2|^2 - |d1|^2) / (2 |d2 - d1|)`, which is what makes
  flagstones, chips and leather pebbles crisp.
* *Layouts* (ashlar courses, planks, weave, slab border) are computed in
  modular arithmetic, with joints staggered against the previous course.
* *Wrapped drawing* (`WrapCanvas`): scratches and fibres are drawn nine
  times at +-tile offsets and box-filtered down, so strokes continue across
  edges.
* Blurs (`gaussian_filter(mode="wrap")`) and normal derivation (`sobel`,
  `mode="wrap"`) also wrap.

**Maps per set:** `<set>_albedo.jpg` (sRGB), `_normal.jpg` (tangent space,
**OpenGL convention: +X right, +Y up**, i.e. what three.js expects), `_rough`
and `_ao` (grayscale, linear). `bronze_aged` and `iron_rusted` also ship a
`_metal.jpg` (patina/rust = 0). Normals come from the same height field that
drives AO and grime, with a per-material strength. AO is a multi-radius
cavity estimate (`blur(h, r) - h`). Coverage-type effects (patina, rust,
scuffs) are thresholded at percentiles so coverage is predictable.

Material notes:

* `stone_floor` relaxed Voronoi flagstones; grout; faceted chips made from a
  second small Voronoi field (so broken edges look cut, not melted); hairline
  cracks from Perlin zero-contours; pitting; ash in cavities; damp patches
  that also lower roughness.
* `stone_wall` six courses of ashlar, staggered joints, per-block tone and
  tooling marks, corner chipping, soot heavier near each block's top plus
  vertical streaks.
* `stone_plate` one tile = one slab: chamfered edge (forms a groove when
  tiled), double engraved rule with corner lozenges and mid-side ticks; pale
  ash in the grooves keeps it readable at low contrast.
* `wood_dark` five planks along V, butt joints, growth rings with slow sway
  and cathedral arches, pores, medullary flecks, nails at joints.
* `cloth_wool` 2/2 twill, 64 threads per tile, per-thread thickness/tone,
  fibre fuzz. Neutral undyed tone so `material.color` can dye it.
* `bronze_aged`, `iron_rusted`, `parchment`, `wax`, `leather`: see the
  manifest `purpose` strings.

Usage in three.js: set `albedo.colorSpace = SRGBColorSpace`; leave the
others linear (`NoColorSpace`). `wrapS = wrapT = RepeatWrapping`. Use the
normal map as-is (OpenGL). Grayscale JPEGs load as RGB with equal channels,
so they also work as `metalnessMap` (blue channel) and `aoMap` (red).

## Helper sprites (`sprites.py`)

Drawn with supersampled Pillow vectors and numpy fields.

* `ash_particle`, `ember_particle`, `smoke_puff`: 4x4 atlases of 128 px
  cells, straight (non-premultiplied) alpha. Embers are colour-ramped by
  temperature and intended for additive blending; ash and smoke are near-white
  for tinting.
* `glow_radial` (256), `light_shaft` (256x1024, fades in at the top and out
  toward the bottom): white, dithered against banding.
* `stained_glass` (1024x2048): equilateral lancet, diamond quarries with
  ruby node squares, three medallions (jewelled band, quatrefoil, rosette), a
  border band, lead came derived from label-map edges, iron saddle bars,
  broken holes (alpha 0, some came left hanging), lost panes and cracks.
  Glass alpha 0.94, lead 1.
* `rune_ring`, `holy_ring` (512): white on transparent with a soft glow
  halo. The rune glyphs are original stave-and-branch figures; the inner
  figure is a {7/3} heptagram (seven lines).
* `crack_decal` (512), `blood_decal` (256): dark decals with soft edges.
* `vignette` (1024), `grain` (256, tileable, grayscale around mid-grey).
* `ui_parchment_panel` (1024): dark leather/parchment with a faint blind-tooled
  double rule at 22/29 px; use 9-slice insets of about 40 px.
* `ui_frame_corner` (256): top-left bronze corner, symmetric about the
  diagonal; the two rules run off the right and bottom edges so the 9-slice
  edges can stretch them. Mirror horizontally/vertically for other corners
  (the baked light comes from the top-left).

## Icon technique

Icons are authored in Python as geometry on a 48x48 grid: primitives
(circles, rounded rects, stroked polylines, cubic/quadratic paths, arcs,
stars) combined with shapely booleans. Two operations give the engraved,
heraldic look:

* `over(base, top, gap)` lays one part over another with a carved gap, so
  overlapping elements stay legible in a single colour;
* `cut(shape, lines)` engraves details (fullers, facets, stitching) out of a
  silhouette.

Each icon is flattened into one `<path fill="currentColor"
fill-rule="evenodd">` (no strokes, masks or ids), so it tints with CSS
`color`, renders identically everywhere and works inside the `icons.svg`
sprite (`<svg><use href="/assets/icons/icons.svg#hp"/></svg>`). Main strokes
are 3.2 units (about 1.3 px at 20 px), engraved gaps at least 1.2 units.

## Tests

`test_assets.py` checks: every manifest file exists with the recorded size
and dimensions; power-of-two sizes; texture budget under 20 MB; RGBA sprites
have transparency; tileable maps have no seam (wrap-around step compared with
other JPEG block-boundary steps, image-wide and near the edge; for normal maps
only the component along the seam, since grooves may sit on the tile edge);
the seam metric itself flags non-tileable inputs; raw generator output is
periodic before JPEG; normal maps are unit length, point outward and follow
the OpenGL +Y convention; SVGs are ASCII, valid XML, use `currentColor`, have
no text or hard-coded colours; the sprite has a symbol for every required id;
no two icons are identical.
